classification.difficultyReason: Translate calm and dry into complements, infer an empty outside region, and express exclusive counts using an unknown triple overlap before enforcing the monthly total.

content.prompt: Weather records for July 2010 in Sydney showed that the month had no hot, calm, dry days. Of the 31 days, 7 were wet and cold but not windy, 4 were wet and windy but not cold, 8 were cold and windy but dry. 16 days were windy, 22 were cold and 2 were wet but not cold or windy. If a day is chosen at random. What is the probability that the day was:

answer.short:
$\dfrac{1}{31}$.

Exactly one day lies in all three weather sets.
answer.worked:
Let $x$ be the number of cold, wet and windy days. In a three-set Venn diagram, wet only is 2, wet-and-cold only is 7, wet-and-windy only is 4, and cold-and-windy only is 8. The outside region is 0.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Cold only}&=22-7-8-x\\\text{Cold only}&=7-x\\\text{Windy only}&=16-4-8-x\\\text{Windy only}&=4-x.\end{align*}$$
Summing the disjoint regions:
$$\begin{align*}31&=2+7+4+8+x+(7-x)+(4-x)\\31&=32-x\\x&=1\\P(\text{cold, wet and windy})&=\frac{1}{31}.\end{align*}$$

The cold-only region is $7-x$. From part a, $x=1$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Cold, calm and dry days}&=7-1\\\text{Cold, calm and dry days}&=6\\P(\text{cold but calm and dry})&=\frac{6}{31}.\end{align*}$$
